title: Rope Drop: It's IAAPA week in Orlando
summary:
By Robert Niles: As the "rope drop" starts a day at theme parks, the Sunday "Rope Drop" post kicks off the week here at Theme Park Insider. Here is what lies ahead for fans at the parks this week.

It's time again this week for the theme park industry's largest annual gathering. The IAAPA Expo returns to Orlando this week, with the event taking over both halls of the Orange County Convention Center for the first time. Tuesday is the big day for news from the Expo, with train reveals planned for:

  • Lagoon's Hot Racer, from Intamin
  • Six Flags Magic Mountain's Thrill Glider, from Vekoma
  • Holiday World's Cannonball!, from Mack Rides
  • Kentucky Kingdom's Midnight Showdown, from Gravity Group
  • Silver Dollar City's Miner's Mountain Express, from Mack Rides
  • S & S Worldwide's RailRyder

In addition, Rocky Mountain Coasters is revealing its new family coaster model, Sally Dark Rides is showing off its Mini dark ride concept, and United Parks & Resorts is planning to preview new attractions coming to Busch Gardens and SeaWorld parks. Finally, we expect to hear from VAI Resorts and its new partner Falcon's Beyond about the status of the Mattel Adventure Park in Glendale, Arizona.

The IAAPA Expo starts Monday and continues through Friday. If you are attending, don't miss Bob Rogers' Legends panel on Wednesday at 4pm, in a new location in the West Concourse, The Learning Hub W304-ABCEFG. Joining Bob this year will be Leslie Iwerks, Joe Rohde, and Bob Weis.

Later this week, on Friday, Knott's Merry Farm starts at Knott's Berry Farm, while Universal Kids Resort kicks off its first Holidays at Universal Kids Resort celebration. Both events continue through January 3, 2027.

You can find our list of all upcoming major theme park events and refurbishments at themeparkinsider.com/calendar.

title: Walk Time: Holiday season begins at Universal
summary:
By Robert Niles: "Walk Time" is Theme Park Insider's Saturday look back at theme park news from the past week.

Holidays at Universal Orlando Resort opens today - the latest theme park holiday event to start this season. The resort's traditional holiday entertainment returns, including Christmas in The Wizarding World of Harry Potter, Grinchmas Who-liday Spectacular, and Universal�s Holiday Parade Featuring Macy�s, which will feature a new Earl the Squirrel balloon after it makes its debut at the big show in New York this Thanksgiving Day.

Also this week, holiday celebrations began at Disneyland and Walt Disney World, where we brought you a trip report from the return of Disney Jollywood Nights: Here is what to expect at Walt Disney World's Jollywood Nights.

I visited Disneyland earlier this month to preview Walt Disney Imagineering's new in-park app, which allows Disneyland Magic Key holders to help WDI test "experiments," including a new interactive Star Wars Galaxy's Edge game and an upcoming digital assistant guide to the parks: Introducing Walt Disney Imagineering's new app for theme park fans.

Vote for your favorite attractions

Voting is now open for the 26th annual Theme Park Insider Awards. Your ranking of the world's top attractions also will determine the rides, shows and other experiences that Theme Park Insider recommends on its theme park visitors guide pages. To vote, just submit your ranking of up to 40 favorite attractions around the world, in order, at themeparkinsider.com/vote. Or, if you don't want to fuss with the submission form, just email your list to me at themeparkinsider@gmail.com.

Attractions can be dark rides, roller coasters, shows, parades, nighttime spectaculars, track rides, play areas, meet and greets - anything that you consider an attraction worth recommending to other theme park fans around the world. Voting closes in early December and I will announce the winners in January. Thank you for voting!

New gigs

Former Disneyland President and Cedar Fair CEO Matt Ouimet has joined the board of directors at Herschend. That's a great add for the family-owned company as it continues to grow. Herschend recently bought several former Palace Entertainment parks from Parques Reunidos, and Dollywood posted the biggest percentage attendance gain among U.S. theme parks in the most recent TEA attendance report.

Six Flags has hired Adam Boal as chief procurement officer. Boal joins Six Flags from CBRE and before that, AstraZeneca, where he oversaw procurement strategy and supplier partnerships.

BRC Imagination Arts has a new client in The Muhammad Ali Center. BRC will reimagine the Louisville center, which welcomes more than 80,000 visitors a year.

"We chose BRC because they share our belief that a story told with heart can change how people live, and because they understand that the Center should carry Muhammad�s values into everyday life," Lonnie Ali, Muhammad Ali's wife and the co-founder of the center, said. "We want this message to reach young people everywhere and to travel further than it ever has."

For more theme park news, please sign up for Theme Park Insider's free weekly newsletter.

title: Construction goes vertical on new Six Flags coaster
summary:
By Robert Niles: Six Flags Magic Mountain has installed the first track pieces for its new Thrill Glider roller coaster.

The world's first installation of this new coaster model from Vekoma is "on track" to open next year at Magic Mountain. The coaster is going in on and around the site of the park's former Golden Bear Theatre.

Six Flags knows how much fans love POV videos, so here is a video from the POV of the first track support to go vertical.

Thrill Glider will be 3,380 feet long, with multiple launches and a top speed of 50 mph. The coaster will top out at 107 feet and feature five inversions: a wing-over, zero-g roll, overbanked stall turn, barrel roll, and upward barrel roll.

Six Flags is theming the coaster to "The Futurist Pavilion," a showcase for "QuantumPulse Propulsion Systems," which has discovered a new energy source collected from distant pulsars. Along the course, riders will pass through hexagonal decorations that will collect that energy, in Six Flags' story for the ride.

You can browse a list of other major attractions coming to theme park around the world over the next few years on our Plan ahead for new theme park attractions page.

title: The 2026 holiday season kicks off at Disney
summary:
By Robert Niles: Merry Disney Christmas to theme park fans across the United States today.

The Holidays at Walt Disney World and Holidays at the Disneyland Resort events kicked off today, officially starting the Christmas season at Disney's U.S. theme parks.

In California, Disneyland is bringing back its traditional slate of holiday attractions, including overlays at It's a Small World, Redwood Creek Challenge Trail, and Cars Land, with Haunted Mansion holiday continuing from Halloween. The Believe in Holiday Magic fireworks show is back, as is the A Christmas Fantasy parade, which is running for its 31st year. Festival of Holidays and �Viva Navidad! also return at Disney California Adventure this year.

At Walt Disney World, fans can find new holiday music overlays on the Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring The Muppets roller coasters this year. Jingle Cruise and Frozen Holiday Surprise return at the Magic Kingdom, but the big holiday events at WDW are the after-hours parties: Mickey's Very Merry Christmas Party and Disney Jollywood Nights.

Over at EPCOT, the EPCOT International Festival of the Holidays does not start until after Thanksgiving. Starting November 27, it will be time again for the Candlelight performance and Holiday Kitchens food booths.

Disney's holiday celebrations continue daily through January 6, 2027. Elsewhere, the Holidays at Universal Orlando Resort starts tomorrow, while you can find our list of other theme park holiday celebrations around the country on our theme park calendar page.

For more theme park news, please sign up for Theme Park Insider's free weekly newsletter.

title: Disneyland fixes one of its biggest mistakes
summary:
By Robert Niles: Finally, someone at Disneyland has come to their senses. The park is now serving its most popular coffee drink at breakfast.

Disneyland visitors now may order a Cold Brew Black Caf during breakfast hours at Ronto Roasters in Star Wars Galaxy's Edge. The drink previously had been available starting with lunch hours in the Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo restaurant next door.

This change means that Disneyland fans now can order the dream breakfast of a Ronto Morning Wrap and a Cold Brew Black Caf in one place, and from park opening.

Of all of Disney's attempts to replicate the success of Universal's Butterbeer, I think that the Star Wars cold brew has come closest. The drink features Joffrey's cold brew, topped with sweet cream cheese and cocoa puffed cereal. I am not a fan of Joffrey's - or coffee in general - but I cannot deny that this is one tasty drink.

And the Ronto Morning Wrap has been one of my two go-to breakfast selections at Disneyland, along with the Breakfast Chimichanga from Ship to Shore - the food stand across from Big Thunder Mountain and next to the Mark Twain landing. Yet with the cold brew now available, this pushes Ronto Roasters to the top of my preferred breakfast list at the park.

title: Universal has a new plan to control what you hear in a theme park
summary:
By Robert Niles: Universal is proposing a new way to control the soundscape of its theme parks.

At a Disneyland media event last week, several of us were trying to remember when theme parks first started using background music. Now, music has been an integral part of amusement parks from the beginning. Bands, calliopes, and solo musicians have been playing in amusement parks since long before theme parks started installing speakers through their facilities.

But when did speaker-driven BGM start? We could not come up with an answer, though the opening of Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom was the leading consensus candidate.

BGM is great for setting a mood, but the system fails during parades and special events, when another source of audio takes over a space. The traditional solution has been to turn off the land-based BGM, or to break an area into zones where speakers play the music for whatever float is timed to be passing through that zone at the moment.

Universal has a new patent application this week that tweaks that approach. In "System and Method for Three-Dimensional Control of Noise Emission in an Interactive Space," the company describes its proposal for managing the output of speakers when one comes within a designated distance of another.

Rather than simply using timing, Universal's system uses feedback microphones and 3D modelers to determine which speakers in an area should be playing which tracks, and how loudly. Here is the flow chart from Universal's patent application:


From Universal's patent application

The result should be a smoother and more pleasing transition from one audio track to another as an attraction moves through the park.

You can read the full details of Universal's proposal in its patent application: System and Method for Three-Dimensional Control of Noise Emission in an Interactive Space.

title: Voting is now open for the 2027 Theme Park Insider Awards
summary:
By Robert Niles: It's time again to vote for the annual Theme Park Insider Awards.

I would like to invite all Theme Park Insider readers to participate. To nominate your favorite attractions for this year's awards, just go to themeparkinsider.com/vote.

That page will ask you to rank up to 40 of your favorite attractions from around the world, starting with your favorite at number one. You do not need to submit 40 attractions - that's just the upper limit for the form. Just submit the attractions that you feel are worthy of being recommended to other Theme Park Insider readers.

If you don't wish to bother with the form, please just email me your list of nominees, ranked from the top on down. You can send that list to themeparkinsider@gmail.com.

I will tally all the submissions and the aggregate ranking will determine this year's Theme Park Insider Award winners, as well as the recommended attractions on our theme park visitors guides.

Voting will close in one month, on December 11, but it's a huge help to me if you get your ballot in early.

Thank you for reading and a special thank you in advance to everyone who votes. Your insight and experience help make Theme Park Insider's recommendations so valuable to so many theme park fans around the world.
